claim: AWS Managed Microsoft AD Standard and Enterprise Editions create new managed AD domains that act as resource forests with trust relationships to existing AD domains on premises, in AWS or in other clouds; user identities stay in the existing domains while the resource forest manages the AWS resources.

values.display: establish resource forests
User identities stay in your existing AD domains

qualifiers.scope: AWS Managed Microsoft AD Standard Edition and Enterprise Edition

evidence.quote: These directories establish resource forests that create trust relationships with your existing AD domains on-premises, in AWS, or in multi-cloud environments. Users can access AWS resources with their existing credentials from your current AD domains. User identities stay in your existing AD domains while the resource forest manages your AWS resources, maintaining operational isolation between environments while providing seamless single sign-on.

claim: AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Hybrid Edition) connects a self-managed Active Directory with AWS Directory Service and extends directory services to AWS without synchronizing user identities, using trust relationships and existing credentials.

values.display: connects your self-managed Active Directory

evidence.quote: This solution extends your directory services to AWS without synchronizing user identities, establishes trust relationships between environments, and provides seamless access using existing credentials.

Directory Service offers two Microsoft Active Directory solutions: *AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory* provides a fully managed Active Directory service in the AWS Cloud, while *AWS Managed Microsoft AD (Hybrid Edition)* extends your existing self-managed AD to AWS.

note: d085. Hybrid Edition is a recent addition; GA date for the numbers+changes lens; likely not on the exam.

claim: AD Connector does not support Active Directory transitive trusts; AD Connectors and on-premises domains have a 1-to-1 relationship, so each on-premises domain, including child domains, needs its own AD Connector.
question: Does one AD Connector cover all domains of an on-premises forest?

values.display: does not support Active Directory transitive trusts
have a 1-to-1 relationship
you must create a unique AD Connector

evidence.quote: AD Connector does not support Active Directory transitive trusts. AD Connectors and your on-premises Active Directory domains have a 1-to-1 relationship. That is, for each on-premises domain, including child domains in an Active Directory forest that you want to authenticate against, you must create a unique AD Connector.

claim: AD Connector cannot be shared with other AWS accounts (AWS suggests sharing AWS Managed Microsoft AD instead), and it is not multi-VPC aware, so applications such as WorkSpaces must be provisioned in the same VPC as the AD Connector.
question: Can an AD Connector be shared with other accounts or used from other VPCs?

values.display: cannot be shared with other AWS accounts
not multi-VPC aware
the same VPC as your AD Connector

evidence.quote: AD Connector cannot be shared with other AWS accounts. If this is a requirement, consider using AWS Managed Microsoft AD to [Share your AWS Managed Microsoft AD](ms_ad_directory_sharing.md). AD Connector is also not multi-VPC aware, which means that AWS applications like [WorkSpaces](https://aws.amazon.com/workspaces) are required to be provisioned into the same VPC as your AD Connector.
